newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-KEN GRIFFEY JR HAS HAMSTRING STRAIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-KEN GRIFFEY JR HAS HAMSTRING STRAIN.

text.p: Seattle Mariners superstar centre fielder Ken Griffey Jr, seemingly poised to make another charge at the single-season home run record of 61, has run into yet another injury.

Griffey, who has 29 homers in just 75 games, suffered the injury, initially diagnosed as tightness in his right hamstring, running out a double in the bottom of the first inning of the Mariners' 9-4 win over the Oakland Athletics Wednesday night.
He was expected to be re-examined on Thursday with a decision to be made on his status at that time.
The 27-year-old Griffey is hitting .315 with 79 RBI. He has led the Mariners to a 44-32 record and a 3 1/2-game lead in the American League West.

Griffey, who has 267 homers and 804 RBI in career 1,132 games, missed three weeks last season with a broken bone in his right wrist. In 1995 he sat out 73 games with a broken wrist suffered by running into the Kingdome fence.
Griffey also broke a bone in the little finger of his right hand in 1992, causing him to miss nearly a month of that season.

Griffey has received more than 2 million All-Star votes and leads all American League players. The seven-time All-Star, who has been the top vote-getter three times since 1991, has nearly double the total votes of any other A.L. outfielder.
